relations.rationale: Rosa adjusting the lighting rig is a separate action from checking her watch, with no logical link between them.
Adjusting a lighting rig has no bearing on anyone's height.
Rosa adjusting the rig before others settled in is unrelated to the cast later gathering their things.
Noor not being in Hugo's class and Kai not being in Hugo's class describe different people's class relations to Hugo and neither implies the other.
Noor's class membership relative to Hugo has no connection to a statement about theater closing times.
Ana arriving earlier than Hugo does not determine her arrival relative to Kai.
Ana's arrival time relative to Hugo has no bearing on whether the group has limited time left.
Arrival order has no logical connection to physical height.
Ana arriving before Hugo doesn't relate to where Hugo practices his lines.
Ana's arrival time relative to Hugo is unrelated to the stage lights dimming later.
Ana arriving later than Kai has no bearing on the stage lights dimming.
Ana taking photographs is unrelated to the cast gathering their belongings.
Running through the act twice before break plausibly leads to increased confidence in blocking through repetition.
Being asked to run through the act twice before a break suggests time pressure, supporting the idea of limited time.
The instruction to run through the act twice is unrelated to the specific detail of lights dimming at the end.
The cast's growing confidence in blocking has no bearing on class membership of Kai and Hugo.
Growing confidence in blocking during rehearsal is consistent with the run-through ending, which is when lights dimmed, but doesn't directly cause it.
Kai and Hugo's class assignment has no bearing on whether the group has limited time.
Rosa checking her watch could plausibly precede or relate to her reminding others of the early closing time, though not strictly implied.
Rosa checking her watch suggests concern about time, supporting the idea that they have limited time left.
